title: Do not select unavailable Skills for Agent execution
goal: Ensure Agent-driven Skill selection only considers Skills with a resolvable executor, and explicit execution fails clearly before policy prompts when the selected Skill is unavailable.
context: SkillRuntime.select intentionally operates on manifests and does not require an executor because it is also a generic selection API. SkillAgentOrchestrator.run currently passes every Skill in the Agent manifest to that selector. An imported Skill with no executor can win intent matching; execution then throws unknownSkill and M8 runChatSkillIfMatched does not treat that as no match, so normal chat fallback is interrupted. Filter to executor-available Skill IDs in the Agent execution path without changing generic SkillRuntime.select semantics. The M6 integration regression test now asserts that an unavailable imported Skill yields no selection/falls back, while still asserting that no file is created and no workspace write module is invoked.
forbidden_changes: Do not change generic SkillRuntime.select behavior or manifest discovery.
Do not bypass policy, approval, Agent scope, schema validation, cancellation, or verification.
Do not make unsupported Skills executable or weaken fail-closed behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Agent run selects only among Skills whose executorAvailability is available.
When no in-scope Skill is executable/matching, Agent run returns noSelection so M8 chat can continue normal fallback.
Explicit Agent execute of an unavailable Skill throws a dedicated unavailableSkill error before policy or executor side effects.
Agent manifests with stale Skill IDs are still rejected before selection.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on final PR head.
recovery: Revert this single logical change if selection or policy regressions occur; preserve generic manifest-only selection and fail-closed execution.
